home.title: What Time Is It? Live Clock and Today's Date | Saat Tarih
home.description: What time is it now and what's today's date? See your live local time, the date, the week number and the time in cities around the world on one page.
home.lead: Saat Tarih is a free website that shows your local time, today's date, the week number and the time in cities around the world, live. For everyone, no sign-up needed. Swipe between {n} clock styles and show any of them full screen.
home.worldHeading: Time in cities around the world
home.worldLead: Current local time in selected cities. Select a city for details.

faq.q: How is the time on this site calculated?
faq.a: The time is synchronised with the site's server, so it is right even if your device clock is wrong. The time zone is read from your device settings. Synchronisation sends only a few small requests to the server and no personal data.

faq.q: Does Türkiye use daylight saving time?
faq.a: No. Since 2016 Türkiye has used UTC+3 all year round, and clocks are not moved forward or back. Many European countries still change their clocks, so their time difference from Türkiye can shift by one hour during the year.

faq.q: How is the week number calculated?
faq.a: Under ISO 8601, weeks start on Monday and week 1 is the week that contains the first Thursday of the year. For this reason the first and last days of a year can belong to a week of the neighbouring year.

faq.q: How is the time difference between cities worked out?
faq.a: Each city's current UTC offset comes from your browser's time zone database (IANA), and daylight saving changes are applied automatically. "Ahead of you" and "behind you" always refer to your own time zone.

faq.q: How do I change the clock style?
faq.a: Swipe left or right on the clock; on a computer use the dots below it or the arrow keys on your keyboard. The styles include classic and minimal analogue, digital, analogue and digital together, versions with or without the date, clocks with a monthly calendar, a flip clock, a clock in words, a ring clock and a big date. Your choice is remembered on this device.

faq.q: How do I see the clock full screen?
faq.a: Press the full screen button under the clock. To leave, press the same button or the Esc key. You can keep swiping between styles in full screen too.

faq.q: Does the clock work independently of my device clock?
faq.a: Yes. The time is synchronised with the site's server, so it shows the correct time even if your device clock is wrong, and it tells you how far your device clock is off. The time zone is still read from your device settings.

faq.q: Where can I see Turkish public holidays and Ramadan?
faq.a: The yearly calendar page shows public holidays, bayram and eve days, kandil nights and the month of Ramadan on one calendar. The "Upcoming days" section at the top of the calendar page tells you how many days are left until the next holiday.

privacy.title: Privacy and Cookie Policy | Saat Tarih
privacy.description: What data Saat Tarih processes, how cookies and local storage are used, Umami statistics, the email list and your rights under Turkish data protection law (KVKK).
privacy.lead: This page explains which data is processed when you use Saat Tarih, why, and what your rights are. The site only collects what it needs; there are no accounts, ads or tracking cookies.

p: The data controller is Bumba Teknoloji Limited Şirketi (Ataşehir / Istanbul, Türkiye). For any question or data protection request: [bilgi@bumbagroup.com](mailto:bilgi@bumbagroup.com).

ul: **Time and date:** Your device's time and time zone are read and calculated only in your browser. They are not sent to a server or stored.

**Location (prayer times):** If you press "Use my location" on the prayer times page, your browser uses your location only on your device to calculate the times. The coordinates are not sent to the server or included in statistics; your last choice stays in your browser's local storage.

**Weather:** On the weather page (or if you turn on the weather in full screen or pick a clock style with weather), the approximate coordinates of the province or location you chose (to about 1 km) are sent straight from your browser to Open-Meteo (api.open-meteo.com), which provides the data. The Saat Tarih server does not see or store these coordinates; Open-Meteo's own privacy terms apply.

**Map (globe):** If you zoom the globe on the home page beyond a certain level, map tiles are downloaded straight to your browser from OpenStreetMap's server (tile.openstreetmap.org); your IP address and the tile addresses of the area you are looking at then reach the OpenStreetMap Foundation. This request is not made when the page first opens or while the globe is zoomed out. The Saat Tarih server does not see them; OpenStreetMap's own privacy terms apply.

**Email list form:** The email address you enter, the consent you give with the checkbox, the selected language and the page of the form are processed by Bumba Group's shared list service (bumbagroup.com). Sign-up uses double opt-in: you are not added until you click the link in the confirmation email, and every email contains a one-click unsubscribe link. See the [shared privacy notice](https://bumbagroup.com/liste/aydinlatma?dil=en) for details.

**Server logs:** The server that hosts the site keeps a standard access log for each request, with the IP address, browser information, the requested page and the time. These logs are used only for security and troubleshooting, not to build profiles of people.

**Visit statistics:** Umami, which runs on our own server, counts page views and a few actions (language change, theme change, whether a search found a result, joining the list). Umami does not use cookies. The words you type in search and your email address are not sent to the statistics system.

**Time synchronisation:** To show the time independently of your device clock, your browser sends a few small requests to the site's own server and reads the date header of the reply. These requests only appear in the server's standard access log; nothing extra is sent.

p: Saat Tarih does not set any cookies, so we do not show a cookie banner. To remember your choices we use your browser's local storage (localStorage); this stays on your device and is not sent to a server. You can delete it at any time in your browser settings.

Server logs and visit statistics: our legitimate interest in keeping the site secure and working (KVKK art. 5/2-f).

stopwatch.title: Online Stopwatch with Laps and Full Screen | Saat Tarih
stopwatch.description: Free online stopwatch: lap times, best and slowest lap, full screen and keyboard shortcuts. Your time is kept even if you reload the page.
stopwatch.lead: The stopwatch is accurate to a hundredth of a second, records lap times and keeps your time even if you reload or close and reopen the page. Space starts and stops it, L adds a lap.
stopwatch.hint: Shortcuts: Space start/stop, L lap, R reset.

faq.q: How accurate is the stopwatch?
faq.a: Time is measured with the browser's high-resolution clock and shown to a hundredth of a second. Changing your device clock does not affect it.

faq.q: Will I lose my time if I close the page?
faq.a: No. The start time of a running stopwatch is stored on this device, so reloading or reopening the page shows the time where it left off. The Reset button clears it.

faq.q: What is a lap and how do I record one?
faq.a: A lap is a split time taken without stopping the stopwatch. Press the Lap button or the L key while it runs; each lap time and the total are listed, with the best and slowest laps marked.

countdown.title: Countdown Timer: By Duration or Date | Saat Tarih
countdown.description: Free countdown: a minute timer or the time left until a date you choose. Countdown to New Year and bayram, sound alert and full screen.
countdown.lead: The countdown works in two ways: a timer that alerts you when your chosen duration ends, or a live display of the days, hours and seconds left until a date you pick. Count down to New Year, a bayram or your own date.
countdown.invalid: Enter a valid duration or a date in the future.

faq.q: What happens when the countdown ends?
faq.a: A sound alert plays, the page title flashes and, if you allowed it, a notification appears. Stop the alert with the Close button.

faq.q: How do I count down to a specific date?
faq.a: On the Until a date tab, pick the target date and time or press one of the quick targets such as New Year and the bayrams. Days, hours, minutes and seconds update live.

faq.q: Does the countdown keep running if I close the tab?
faq.a: The countdown is stored on this device, so reopening the page shows the correct time left. The sound alert cannot play while the page is closed.

countdown.shareNote: You can share the link for the date you picked; the countdown starts by itself when the link is opened.

alarm.title: Online Alarm Clock: Repeating and Snooze | Saat Tarih
alarm.description: Free alarm that runs in your browser: time, label, repeat on chosen weekdays, 5-minute snooze and notifications. The alarm rings while the page is open.
alarm.lead: Choose an alarm time and the days you want; when the time comes a sound plays and a notification appears. Alarms are stored on this device. Because of browser limits, the alarm only rings while this page (tab) stays open.
alarm.wakeNote: If the screen turns off the browser may put the tab to sleep; this option stops the screen from turning off while an alarm is set.
alarm.note: For important wake-ups also set your phone's own alarm; a browser alarm will not ring if the page is closed.

faq.q: Will the alarm ring if I close the tab?
faq.a: No. Websites cannot play sound while the page is closed. This page must stay open in a tab and the device must stay awake; the Keep the screen on option helps with that.

faq.q: Does the alarm depend on my device clock?
faq.a: No. The alarm is checked against a clock synchronised with the server, so it rings at the right moment even if your device clock is a few seconds off. The time zone comes from your device.

faq.q: How do I snooze the alarm?
faq.a: While it rings, press Snooze 5 min and it rings again five minutes later. The Close button silences it; repeating alarms ring again on the next chosen day.

pomodoro.title: Pomodoro Timer: Work 25 Minutes, Break 5 | Saat Tarih
pomodoro.description: Free pomodoro timer: 25 minutes of work, a 5-minute short break and a long break every 4 rounds. Adjustable times, sound alerts and full screen.
pomodoro.lead: The Pomodoro technique alternates 25 minutes of focused work with 5-minute short breaks, followed by a long break after 4 rounds. The times can be changed and a sound plays at each switch.

faq.q: What is the Pomodoro technique?
faq.a: Developed by Francesco Cirillo, it has you work without interruption for 25 minutes and then take a 5-minute break. After four work rounds you take a longer break of 15 to 30 minutes.

faq.q: Can I change the durations?
faq.a: Yes. You can set the work, short break and long break lengths and the number of rounds before a long break; the settings are stored on this device.

faq.q: Do the phases switch automatically?
faq.a: Yes. When time is up a sound plays and the next phase (work or break) starts by itself. Press Pause to stop.

week.title: What Week Is It? ISO Week Number and Dates | Saat Tarih
week.description: Which week of the year is it now? The ISO week number, this week's date range, every week of {year} and a tool to find the week number of any date.
week.lead: Saat Tarih shows live which week of the year it is under ISO 8601. Weeks start on Monday and week 1 is the week that contains the first Thursday of the year. {year} has {weeks} weeks.
week.findHeading: Find the week number of a date

week.faqHeading: Frequently asked questions about week numbers

faq.q: Which week of the year is it now?
faq.a: The live counter above shows today's week number. It follows ISO 8601: weeks start on Monday and week 1 is the week that contains the first Thursday of the year.

faq.q: How many weeks are in a year?
faq.a: An ISO year has 52 or 53 weeks. It has 53 weeks when 1 January is a Thursday (or a Wednesday in a leap year). {year} has {weeks} weeks.

faq.q: Why is 1 January sometimes in the last week of the previous year?
faq.a: Under ISO rules, week 1 contains the first Thursday. If 1 January is a Friday, Saturday or Sunday it belongs to week 52 or 53 of the previous year, and some days at the end of December can belong to week 1 of the next year.

faq.q: What is the week number used for?
faq.a: Week numbers are not much used in daily life, but ISO week numbers are common in business planning, logistics, education and software. The tool on this page shows the week number of any date you pick.

tz.title: Does Türkiye Have Daylight Saving Time? UTC+3 Explained | Saat Tarih
tz.description: Does Türkiye observe daylight saving time? Türkiye has used UTC+3 all year round since 2016. Time differences and DST status for cities around the world.
tz.h1: Does Türkiye have daylight saving time?
tz.lead: No. Since 2016 Türkiye has used the UTC+3 time zone all year round; clocks are not moved forward or back in summer or winter. The zone is called Türkiye Time (TRT) and its IANA identifier is Europe/Istanbul.
facts: Clocks are not changed twice a year
history: Until 2016 Türkiye used UTC+2 in winter (Eastern European Time) and UTC+3 in summer (Eastern European Summer Time).
A 2016 decision made summer time permanent; Türkiye has stayed on UTC+3 all year round since then.
tz.tableHeading: Time difference between Türkiye and cities around the world
tz.tableCaption: Standard time difference from Türkiye time and daylight saving status
tz.note: The standard difference is the difference when daylight saving is not in effect. For cities that observe daylight saving it changes by one hour for part of the year; the "Right now" column shows today's actual difference.
tz.faqHeading: Frequently asked questions about the Türkiye time zone

faq.q: Does Türkiye observe daylight saving time?
faq.a: No. Türkiye made summer time permanent in 2016; UTC+3 is used all year and clocks are not moved forward or back.

faq.q: Which time zone is Türkiye in?
faq.a: Türkiye is in the UTC+3 time zone, known as Türkiye Time (TRT); its IANA identifier is Europe/Istanbul.

faq.q: Is the time difference with Europe the same all year?
faq.a: No. Many European countries observe daylight saving time, so their difference from Türkiye changes by one hour during the year. The table above shows today's difference.

faq.q: What does UTC+3 mean?
faq.a: UTC+3 means three hours ahead of Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). When it is 12:00 UTC, it is 15:00 in Türkiye.

converter.title: Time Converter: Convert Time Between Cities | Saat Tarih
converter.description: Convert the time in one city to the time in another. A time converter for cities worldwide that applies daylight saving time automatically.
converter.lead: Pick the source and target city and a date and time; the matching time appears instantly. Daylight saving changes are applied automatically.
converter.result: When it is {fromTime} in {from}, it is {toTime} in {to}.
converter.faqHeading: Frequently asked questions about the time converter

faq.q: How does the time converter work?
faq.a: It converts the date and time in the source city to universal time using that city's time zone, then applies the target city's time zone. Daylight saving changes come from your browser's time zone database.

faq.q: Does daylight saving time affect the difference?
faq.a: Yes. For cities that observe daylight saving time the difference changes by one hour for part of the year. The converter uses the real difference on the date you pick.

faq.q: What does My location mean?
faq.a: It uses your device's time zone, so you can convert the time where you are to another city.

planner.title: Meeting Planner: Find Overlapping Working Hours | Saat Tarih
planner.description: Find the best meeting time across time zones. Working hours, early or late hours and night hours are colour-coded for every city.
planner.lead: Add cities and pick a date; each city's hourly timeline appears side by side. Overlapping working hours (09:00–18:00) are found automatically.
planner.noCommon: The selected cities have no overlapping working hours; pick the least inconvenient hours from the timeline.
planner.faqHeading: Frequently asked questions about the meeting planner

faq.q: How are overlapping working hours found?
faq.a: Working hours are taken as 09:00–18:00 in each city. Hours when all selected cities are at work at the same time are marked green and listed.

faq.q: Is daylight saving time taken into account?
faq.a: Yes. The real time differences on the date you pick are used, so daylight saving changes are applied automatically.

faq.q: How many cities can I add?
faq.a: You can add up to six cities. Your selection is stored on this device.

datecalc.faqHeading: Frequently asked questions about date calculations

faq.q: How are the days between two dates calculated?
faq.a: You subtract the start date from the end date; the calculator does this automatically and also shows the result in weeks and in years, months and days.

faq.q: Do working days exclude public holidays?
faq.a: The working-day count leaves out weekends and Turkish public holidays; bayram eve half days count as 0.5 working days. Holiday data is the 2026–2031 data from our calendar pages.

faq.q: How is age calculated?
faq.a: The completed years, months and days from the date of birth to today are counted. The calculator also shows the total days lived and the days until the next birthday.

faq.q: How is the end of the month handled when adding months?
faq.a: If the target month does not have that day, its last day is used; for example adding 1 month to 31 January gives the last day of February.

faq.q: How are prayer times calculated?
faq.a: The position of the sun during the day is calculated from your latitude and longitude. Fajr starts when the sun is 18° below the horizon, isha at 17° below, and asr when an object's shadow equals its length. The calculation runs in your browser.

faq.q: Is my location sent to the server?
faq.a: No. If you allow location access, the coordinates are used only on your device to calculate the times; they are not sent to the server or included in statistics events. Your last choice is kept only in your browser's local storage.

faq.q: Are the times the same as Diyanet's?
faq.a: The calculation is tuned to match Diyanet's times and differs by at most 1 minute at province centres. Official times are still the ones published by the Turkish Presidency of Religious Affairs.

faq.q: What are the iftar and suhoor times?
faq.a: Iftar is at the maghrib (evening adhan) time, and suhoor runs until fajr (imsak). In Ramadan you can check both in the monthly table.

faq.q: Can I use it abroad?
faq.a: Yes. The Use my location button calculates the times anywhere in the world. At very high latitudes the fajr or isha angle may not occur; then an approximate time is given with the one-seventh-of-the-night rule.

nature.title: Seasons: Seasons Wheel, Equinoxes and Solstices | Saat Tarih
nature.description: Seasons wheel (summer on top), equinox and solstice dates, the longest day and night, sunrise and sunset, the Moon's phase and day length through the year.
nature.lead: The year turns like a wheel: which season are we in, how many days to the next one, when does the sun rise and set, and what phase is the Moon? All on one page for your location or a province you choose.
nature.dayLonger: The day is {m} min longer than yesterday
nature.dayShorter: The day is {m} min shorter than yesterday
nature.tableLead: Astronomical seasons, that is the moments of the equinoxes and solstices. Times are in Turkey time (UTC+3).
nature.meteoNote: Meteorological seasons are three-month blocks: spring starts on 1 March, summer on 1 June, autumn on 1 September and winter on 1 December. They are used for calendars and statistics.

spring: Day and night are equal at the equinox, and over the following months the days lengthen quickly.
Flowers bloom and trees turn green; migratory birds return north.
Snow melts and rivers rise; the soil is made ready for sowing.
summer: The longest day of the year falls on the summer solstice.
The sea and the soil warm up, and the season for fruit and vegetables peaks.
Short nights and clear skies make this the best time to watch the Milky Way.
autumn: Day and night become equal again, and the days begin to shorten.
Leaves change colour and fall; birds such as storks and cranes migrate south.
It is harvest time: grapes, walnuts, hazelnuts and chestnuts are gathered.
winter: The shortest day of the year falls on the winter solstice, after which the days lengthen again.
Many animals hibernate and plants go dormant.
Snow in the mountains stores the water for spring and summer.

why: Seasons are caused by the Earth's rotation axis being tilted by about 23.4° relative to its orbit around the Sun, not by its distance from the Sun.
When the axis leans toward the Sun, that hemisphere gets more direct light and longer days, and it is summer. When it leans away, it is winter.
At the equinoxes (around 20 March and 22 September) day and night are almost equal; at the solstices (around 21 June and 21 December) the day is the longest or the shortest.
nature.hemisphereNote: Seasons are reversed in the southern hemisphere; if your location is in the south, the season names change accordingly.
nature.methodNote: The sun, Moon and season moments are calculated in your browser with astronomical formulas: season moments to within a few minutes, the Moon's phase and times approximately.
nature.weatherLink: Go to the separate weather page

faq.q: When do the seasons start?
faq.a: Astronomically, spring starts around 20 March, summer on 21 June, autumn on 22-23 September and winter on 21 December. The exact moments shift by a few hours from year to year; see the table above.

faq.q: What is the difference between astronomical and meteorological seasons?
faq.a: Astronomical seasons are based on the equinoxes and solstices, while meteorological seasons use whole calendar months (March to May is spring, for example). The latter makes climate records easier to keep.

faq.q: How does day length change?
faq.a: Day length grows from the winter solstice to the summer solstice and then shortens again. The change is fastest around the equinoxes, by a few minutes a day, and almost still at the solstices.

faq.q: How is the Moon's phase calculated?
faq.a: The phase comes from the time since the previous new moon as a fraction of the lunar cycle (about 29.5 days). New moon and full moon times are calculated with astronomical formulas to within a few minutes.

weather.description: Current weather, an hourly and a 7-day forecast for your location or a province you choose: temperature, feels-like, wind, humidity, rain and UV.

weather.locationNote: The coordinates of the location you choose (to about 1 km) are sent straight from your browser to Open-Meteo, which provides the weather data; the Saat Tarih server does not see them.

faq.q: Where does the weather data come from?
faq.a: The data is downloaded straight to your browser from Open-Meteo, an open weather service. It is a model forecast and can differ from local measurements by a few degrees and hours.

faq.q: Is my location shared?
faq.a: If you choose a location, approximate coordinates (to about 1 km) are sent to Open-Meteo only to fetch the weather. The Saat Tarih server does not see or store them.

faq.q: What is the feels-like temperature?
faq.a: The feels-like temperature is how warm it seems to the body once wind and humidity are taken into account; it can differ from the real air temperature.

faq.q: Can I see the weather on the full-screen clock?
faq.a: Yes. In full screen, the weather button in the bar that appears when you tap the screen shows the weather for your chosen location beside the clock.
